'''Elizabeth A. Stuart''' is a professor of mental health, [[biostatistics]], and health policy and management in the [[Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health]]. Her research involves [[causal inference]] and [[missing data]] in the statistics of mental health. She was a co-author on a study showing that post-suicide-attempt counseling can significantly reduce the risk of future suicide.<ref>[https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2014/11/141124074741.htm Suicide risk falls substantially after talk therapy], Science Daily, November 24, 2014, retrieved 2016-07-19.</ref>

== Education and career==
Stuart graduated from [[Smith College]] in 1997, with a [[mathematics]] major and [[chemistry]] minor.<ref name="cv">[http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~estuart/StuartCV.pdf Curriculum vitae], February 20, 2016, retrieved 2016-07-19.</ref> She completed her Ph.D. at [[Harvard University]] in 2004, in statistics, under the supervision of [[Donald Rubin]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=96507}}</ref> After working for two years as a researcher at [[Mathematica Policy Research]], she joined the Johns Hopkins faculty in 2006.<ref name="cv"/> In 2023, she was promoted to The Frank Hurley and Catharine Dorrier Professor and Chair of the Hopkins Biostatistics department. 

== Recognition ==
In 2014 she was elected as a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Statistical Association]] "for outstanding contributions to research in the estimation of causal effects; for extensive efforts in the dissemination of statistical methods in education and mental health, including the development of widely used software; and for extensive service to the ASA and the profession."<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.amstat.org/newsroom/pressreleases/2014_ASAFellows.pdf|title=ASA Honors 63 New Fellows|publisher=[[American Statistical Association]]|date=June 11, 2014|accessdate=2016-07-11|archive-date=2016-03-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304054602/http://www.amstat.org/newsroom/pressreleases/2014_ASAFellows.pdf|url-status=dead}}.</ref> In 2020, she was elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], in the Section on Statistics.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=AAAS Fellows Elected|department=Mathematics People|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202103/rnoti-p434.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=68|issue=3|page=437|date=March 2021}}</ref> In 2020, she became a Bloomberg Professor of American Health.<ref>{{citation|url=https://publichealth.jhu.edu/2020/elizabeth-stuart-appointed-as-new-bloomberg-professor-of-american-health|title=Elizabeth Stuart Appointed as New Bloomberg Professor of American Health|date=June 11, 2020|publisher=Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health|access-date=2024-12-25}}</ref>
